title: Optimize Slow Database Query
content:
Optimize this slow PostgreSQL query that takes over 30 seconds. The query joins 4 tables and returns analytics data. Include: EXPLAIN ANALYZE interpretation, index recommendations, query rewrite suggestions, partition strategy if applicable, materialized view considerations, and estimated performance improvement for each optimization.

```sql
SELECT u.country, COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) as order_count, SUM(oi.quantity) as total_items
FROM users u
JOIN orders o ON u.id = o.user_id
JOIN order_items oi ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id
WHERE o.created_at > '2023-01-01'
GROUP BY u.country, p.category
ORDER BY order_count DESC;
```

title: Review Database Query Performance
content:
Review this PostgreSQL query and suggest optimizations. The query joins 5 tables, uses multiple subqueries, and takes 45 seconds to execute on a table with 10 million rows.

```sql
SELECT c.customer_name, c.email, o.order_id, o.total,
       p.product_name, p.price, s.shipment_date, s.tracking_number
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN shipments s ON o.order_id = s.order_id
WHERE o.order_date >= '2023-01-01'
  AND o.order_date < '2024-01-01'
  AND p.category_id IN (SELECT category_id FROM categories WHERE category_name = 'Electronics')
ORDER BY o.order_date DESC;
```

title: Optimize slow database queries
content:
Analyze these three PostgreSQL queries and identify performance bottlenecks. For each query, provide: the execution plan interpretation, index recommendations, query rewrite suggestions, and an estimate of performance improvement. Include examples of partial indexes and composite indexes if applicable.

-- Query 1: Active orders with customer details
SELECT o.id, o.created_at, c.name, c.email, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.price) as total
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id
JOIN order_items oi ON o.id = oi.order_id
WHERE o.status = 'active' AND o.created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'
GROUP BY o.id, o.created_at, c.name, c.email;

-- Query 2: Product search with category filter
SELECT p.*, cat.name as category_name
FROM products p
JOIN categories cat ON p.category_id = cat.id
WHERE p.is_active = true AND cat.slug IN ('electronics', 'computers', 'accessories')
ORDER BY p.popularity_score DESC, p.created_at DESC
LIMIT 50;

-- Query 3: Monthly revenue report
SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', created_at) as month, COUNT(*) as orders, SUM(total) as revenue
FROM orders WHERE created_at > '2023-01-01'
GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', created_at);

content:
Analyze this slow-running SQL query and identify the bottleneck. Explain your analysis process step by step: checking the execution plan, identifying missing indexes, understanding table statistics, and evaluating join strategies. Then provide an optimized version with explanation of each change.

Query:
SELECT o.id, o.created_at, u.name, COUNT(oi.id) as item_count
FROM orders o
JOIN users u ON o.user_id = u.id
JOIN order_items oi ON o.id = oi.order_id
WHERE o.created_at > '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY o.id, o.created_at, u.name
ORDER BY o.created_at DESC
LIMIT 100;

FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id
JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
WHERE o.order_date >= '2023-01-01'
GROUP BY o.order_id, o.order_date, c.customer_name

ORDER BY total DESC;
